source_refs.note: Book p. 94-96: 3.6 Definition, Remark, Theorems 3.2 and 3.3 (FTC), Examples 44-48, boxes on substitution and integration by parts for definite integrals

blocks.text: Assalam o alaikum! Ab tak (3.1 se 3.5 tak) hum ne jitne integrals kiye woh sab indefinite the: jawab ek poora khandan (family) hota tha, \(F(x) + c\), jahan \(c\) koi bhi constant ho sakta tha. Aaj hum integral ke nishaan par do numbers likhenge, neeche \(a\) aur upar \(b\). Inhein limits kehte hain. Aur jaise hi limits aa jayein, jawab family nahi rehta balke ek akela number ban jata hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Ek misaal se samjhiye: maan lijiye ek tanki mein paani bhar raha hai. Indefinite integral aap ko batata hai ke kisi bhi waqt tanki mein kitna paani hai, magar shuru mein kitna tha woh maloom nahi (yahi \(+c\) hai). Definite integral sirf yeh poochta hai ke waqt \(a\) se waqt \(b\) tak kitna paani barha. Shuru wala paani dono waqton mein shamil hai, is liye farq nikalte hue khatam ho jata hai.
Achhi khabar yeh hai ke koi naya integration rule nahi seekhna. Standard rules, substitution, integration by parts, partial fractions sab wahi hain. Bas aakhir mein ek qadam barhta hai: limits rakho aur tafreeq (subtract) karo. Aage 3.7 mein yahi number area (raqba) naapega.

blocks.title: Definition
blocks.text:
Let \(f\) be a continuous function on the closed interval \([a, b]\). The definite integral of \(f\) from \(a\) to \(b\) is defined as
\[\int_{a}^{b} f(x)\,dx = F(b) - F(a),\]
where \(F'(x) = f(x)\). Here, \(a\) is the lower limit and \(b\) the upper limit of the integration.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Definition ko aasan alfaaz mein parhiye: pehle \(f\) ka koi bhi antiderivative \(F\) dhoondo (yani aisa function jis ka derivative \(f\) ho). Phir upar wali limit \(b\) us mein rakho, neeche wali limit \(a\) rakho, aur \(F(b) - F(a)\) nikal lo. Bas!
Sharat (condition) yeh hai ke \(f\) poore band interval \([a, b]\) par continuous ho, yani graph mein koi toot ya chhalang na ho. Kitab har jagah yahi farz karti hai.

Remark (kitab ka nukta): definite integral ki value ek real number hoti hai, functions ki family nahi, jaisa ke indefinite integral mein hota tha. Numbers \(a\) aur \(b\) ko limits of integration kehte hain: \(a\) lower limit (neeche wali) aur \(b\) upper limit (upar wali).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Ab sawal yeh hai ke \(+c\) kahan gaya? Chaliye khud dekhte hain. Agar antiderivative \(F(x) + c\) lein to
\[[F(b) + c] - [F(a) + c]\]
\[= F(b) - F(a)\]
Dekha? \(c\) ek dafa plus aur ek dafa minus aaya aur khatam ho gaya. Is liye definite integral mein \(+c\) likhne ki zaroorat hi nahi.
Likhne ka tareeqa: \(\big[F(x)\big]_{a}^{b}\) ka matlab hai \(F(b) - F(a)\). Kai jagah (hamari kitab mein bhi) isi ko seedhi lakeer se \(F(x)\big|_{a}^{b}\) ya \(\big|F(x)\big|_{a}^{b}\) likha jata hai. Dhyan rahe, yeh absolute value (modulus) nahi, sirf limits lagane ka nishaan hai.
Hamari taraf se misaal:
\[\int_{1}^{3} 2x\,dx = \big[x^{2}\big]_{1}^{3}\]
\[= 3^{2} - 1^{2} = 8\]
Khud sochiye: \(\int_{0}^{2} 3x^{2}\,dx\) kitna hoga? (Jawab: \(\big[x^{3}\big]_{0}^{2} = 8 - 0 = 8\).)

blocks.title: Theorem 3.2: First Fundamental Theorem of Calculus (FTC)
blocks.text:
If \(f\) is continuous on \([a, b]\) and \(F(x) = \int_{a}^{x} f(t)\,dt\) for every \(x\) in \([a, b]\), then \(F'(x) = f(x)\), on \([a, b]\).
The derivative with respect to upper limit of the integral of \(f\) is just \(f(x)\).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Is theorem ko aahista aahista parhte hain. Yahan upper limit koi fixed number nahi balke variable \(x\) hai. Integral ke andar \(t\) sirf ek dummy variable (farzi naam) hai; \(t\) ki jagah \(s\) ya \(u\) likh dein, value wahi rahegi.
\(F(x)\) ko aise samjhiye jaise ek meter jo fixed point \(a\) se le kar chalte hue point \(x\) tak \(f\) ka 'jama shuda hissa' (accumulation) ginta ja raha hai. Theorem kehta hai: is jama shuda hisse ka derivative lo to wapas \(f(x)\) mil jata hai.
Matlab differentiation aur integration ek doosre ko 'undo' karte hain, bilkul jaise jama aur tafreeq. Isi liye integration ko anti-differentiation bhi kehte hain.
Hamari taraf se misaal: \(f(t) = t^{2}\) aur \(a = 0\) lein to
\[F(x) = \int_{0}^{x} t^{2}\,dt = \dfrac{x^{3}}{3}\]
\[F'(x) = x^{2} = f(x)\]
Yani \(t\) ki jagah \(x\) aa gaya aur function wapas mil gaya.

blocks.title: Theorem 3.3: Second Fundamental Theorem of Calculus (FTC)
blocks.text:
If \(f\) is continuous on \([a, b]\) and \(F'(x) = f(x)\) on \([a, b]\), then
\[\int_{a}^{b} f(x)\,dx = F(b) - F(a).\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yeh theorem is poore unit mein har definite integral ka asal auzaar (tool) hai. Is ka nuskha (recipe) yaad kar lein:
1. Pehle 3.1 se 3.5 ke rules se koi bhi antiderivative \(F(x)\) nikalein (\(+c\) ki zaroorat nahi).
2. Use square bracket mein limits ke saath likhein: \(\big[F(x)\big]_{a}^{b}\).
3. Pehle upper limit rakhein, phir lower limit, aur tafreeq karein: \(F(b) - F(a)\).
Hamesha 'upar wala minus neeche wala'. Aur \(F(a)\) ko bracket mein band rakhein, taa ke us ke har term ka sign badle. Sab se zyada ghaltiyan isi bracket ko bhoolne se hoti hain.

Ab theory kaafi ho gayi, chaliye kitab ki pehli misaal dekhte hain. Is mein koi chaal nahi, sirf power rule aur limits. Lekin ek jagah, yani negative number ki fractional power, bachay aksar phans jate hain. Is liye har qadam aahista karenge aur har jagah poochenge ke yeh kyun kiya.

blocks.title: Example 44
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int_{-1}^{1} \big(x^{\frac{1}{5}} + 1\big)\,dx\). Lower limit \(a = -1\), upper limit \(b = 1\).
Maloom karna: is definite integral ki value, yani ek number.
Tareeqa: Theorem 3.3 lagayenge. Pehle har term ka antiderivative power rule \(\int x^{n}\,dx = \frac{x^{n+1}}{n+1}\) (\(n \ne -1\)) se nikalenge, phir limits rakh kar tafreeq karenge. Power rule is liye ke dono terms \(x\) ki powers hain (\(1 = x^{0}\)).

Step 1: Har term ka antiderivative
\[\int x^{\frac{1}{5}}\,dx = \dfrac{x^{\frac{1}{5}+1}}{\frac{1}{5}+1}\]
\[= \dfrac{5}{6}\,x^{\frac{6}{5}}\]
\[\int 1\,dx = x\]
Kyun: power rule mein \(n = \frac{1}{5}\) hai. Power mein 1 jama kiya: \(\frac{1}{5} + 1 = \frac{6}{5}\). Phir \(\frac{6}{5}\) se divide karna wahi hai jo \(\frac{5}{6}\) se multiply karna (fraction ulta ho jata hai).
Dhyan dein: \(\frac{1}{5} + 1\) ko \(\frac{2}{5}\) mat likhiye; 1 = \(\frac{5}{5}\), is liye jama \(\frac{6}{5}\) hai.

Step 2: Limits ke saath likhein
\[\int_{-1}^{1} \big(x^{\frac{1}{5}} + 1\big)\,dx\]
\[= \Big[\tfrac{5}{6}x^{\frac{6}{5}} + x\Big]_{-1}^{1}\]
Kyun: Theorem 3.3 ke mutabiq \(F(x) = \frac{5}{6}x^{6/5} + x\) le kar \(F(1) - F(-1)\) nikalna hai. \(+c\) yahan nahi likhte, woh waise bhi kat jata.

Step 3: Har limit par value
\[F(1) = \tfrac{5}{6}(1)^{\frac{6}{5}} + 1 = \tfrac{5}{6} + 1\]
\[F(-1) = \tfrac{5}{6}(-1)^{\frac{6}{5}} + (-1)\]
\[= \tfrac{5}{6} - 1\]
Kyun: \((-1)^{\frac{6}{5}}\) ko do hisson mein dekhiye: pehle fifth root, phir power 6. \(-1\) ka real fifth root \(-1\) hai (kyun ke \((-1)^{5} = -1\)), aur \((-1)^{6} = 1\), kyun ke even power hamesha positive banati hai.
Dhyan dein: bahut se bachay yahan \(-1\) likh dete hain. Power ka numerator 6 even hai, is liye jawab \(+1\) hai.

Step 4: Upar wala minus neeche wala
\[F(1) - F(-1)\]
\[= \Big(\tfrac{5}{6} + 1\Big) - \Big(\tfrac{5}{6} - 1\Big)\]
\[= \tfrac{5}{6} + 1 - \tfrac{5}{6} + 1 = 2\]
Kyun: \(F(-1)\) bracket mein band tha; bracket ke bahar minus ne us ke dono terms ke sign badal diye: \(+\frac{5}{6}\) se \(-\frac{5}{6}\) aur \(-1\) se \(+1\). \(\frac{5}{6}\) aapas mein kat gaye aur \(1 + 1 = 2\) bacha.

Tasdeeq: \(x^{\frac{1}{5}}\) ek odd function hai, kyun ke \((-x)^{\frac{1}{5}} = -x^{\frac{1}{5}}\). Odd function ka \([-1, 1]\) par integral zero hota hai, kyun ke left aur right ke hisse barabar magar ulte sign ke hote hain (yeh Property V hai, agle sabaq 3.6.1 mein). Is liye sirf
\[\int_{-1}^{1} 1\,dx = 1 - (-1) = 2\]
bachta hai. Wahi jawab. \(\checkmark\)

blocks.text: Agli misaal mein integrand pehli nazar mein mushkil lagta hai: neeche \(\sin\theta + \cos\theta\) aur upar \(\sec\theta\). Aise mauqe par ghabrana nahi, balke sochna hai ke kya isay kisi jaani pehchani shakal mein badla ja sakta hai. Sab se kaam ki shakal woh hai jahan upar neeche ka derivative ho, kyun ke us ka jawab seedha \(\ln\) aata hai.

blocks.title: Example 45
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int_{0}^{\pi/4} \frac{\sec\theta}{\sin\theta + \cos\theta}\,d\theta\).
Maloom karna: is ki value.
Tareeqa: integrand ko aisi shakal mein laana hai jahan numerator (upar wala hissa) denominator (neeche wale) ka derivative ho. Aisi soorat mein rule \(\int \frac{f'(\theta)}{f(\theta)}\,d\theta = \ln|f(\theta)| + c\) seedha lag jata hai. Phir limits rakhenge.

Step 1: Denominator mein \(\cos\theta\) common nikalein
\[\sin\theta + \cos\theta = \cos\theta(\tan\theta + 1)\]
Kyun: \(\cos\theta \cdot \tan\theta = \cos\theta \cdot \frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta} = \sin\theta\). Yani bracket khol kar dekhein to wapas \(\sin\theta + \cos\theta\) milta hai. Hum ne yeh is liye kiya ke \(\tan\theta\) ka derivative \(\sec^{2}\theta\) hai, aur \(\sec\theta\) upar pehle se maujood hai.

Step 2: Integrand ko saada karein
\[\dfrac{\sec\theta}{\cos\theta(\tan\theta + 1)}\]
\[= \dfrac{\sec^{2}\theta}{1 + \tan\theta}\]
Kyun: \(\frac{1}{\cos\theta} = \sec\theta\) hota hai, is liye neeche wala \(\cos\theta\) upar ja kar \(\sec\theta\) ban gaya aur pehle wale \(\sec\theta\) ke saath mil kar \(\sec^{2}\theta\) ho gaya.

Step 3: Antiderivative
\[\dfrac{d}{d\theta}(1 + \tan\theta) = \sec^{2}\theta\]
\[\int \dfrac{\sec^{2}\theta}{1 + \tan\theta}\,d\theta\]
\[= \ln|1 + \tan\theta|\]
Kyun: ab upar bilkul neeche wale ka derivative hai, to \(\int \frac{f'}{f} = \ln|f|\) laga diya. Yeh rule kab lagta hai? Jab bhi fraction ka numerator, denominator ka derivative ho (ya us ka constant multiple).

Step 4: Limits rakhein
\[\Big[\ln|1 + \tan\theta|\Big]_{0}^{\pi/4}\]
\[= \ln\Big|1 + \tan\tfrac{\pi}{4}\Big| - \ln|1 + 0|\]
\[= \ln|1 + 1| - 0 = \ln 2\]
Kyun: \(\tan\frac{\pi}{4} = 1\) aur \(\tan 0 = 0\). Aur \(\ln 1 = 0\), kyun ke \(e^{0} = 1\).
Dhyan dein: limits radians mein hain; \(\frac{\pi}{4}\) yani 45 degree.

Tasdeeq (andaze se): \(\theta = 0\) par integrand ki value 1 hai, \(\theta = \frac{\pi}{4}\) par bhi 1, aur beech mein \(\theta = \frac{\pi}{8}\) par taqreeban 0.83. Interval ki chaurai \(\frac{\pi}{4} \approx 0.785\) hai, to jawab 0.785 se thora kam hona chahiye.
\[\ln 2 \approx 0.693\]
bilkul munasib hai, aur numerical integration bhi 0.6931 deta hai. \(\checkmark\)

blocks.text: Teesri misaal mein root ke andar ek expression hai aur bahar \(x\). Jab bhi aap root ya bracket ke andar kuch dekhein aur bahar us ka derivative (ya derivative ka hissa) nazar aaye, to foran samajh jaiye ke power formula ya substitution lagega. Yeh pehchan exam mein bahut waqt bachati hai.

blocks.title: Example 46
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int_{0}^{\sqrt{7}} \frac{x}{\sqrt{x^{2} + 9}}\,dx\).
Maloom karna: is ki value.
Tareeqa: ghor karein, root ke andar \(x^{2} + 9\) hai aur bahar \(x\). \(x^{2} + 9\) ka derivative \(2x\) hai, yani bahar wala \(x\) taqreeban andar wale ka derivative hai (sirf 2 kam hai). Aisi shakal \(\big[f(x)\big]^{n} f'(x)\) ke liye rule hai \(\int [f(x)]^{n} f'(x)\,dx = \frac{[f(x)]^{n+1}}{n+1}\). Phir limits rakhenge.

Step 1: Andar wale function ko naam dein
\[f(x) = x^{2} + 9\]
\[f'(x) = 2x\]
Kyun: rule lagane ke liye \((x^{2} + 9)^{-\frac{1}{2}}\) ke saath poora \(2x\) chahiye; is liye pehle dekh liya ke derivative kya hai.

Step 2: Derivative ko poora karein
\[\int_{0}^{\sqrt{7}} \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{x^{2} + 9}}\,dx\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{2}\int_{0}^{\sqrt{7}} (x^{2} + 9)^{-\frac{1}{2}}(2x)\,dx\]
Kyun: andar 2 se multiply aur bahar \(\frac{1}{2}\) se multiply: kul asar \(2 \times \frac{1}{2} = 1\), yani value nahi badli. Aur \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{u}} = u^{-\frac{1}{2}}\), is liye root ko negative power mein likha.

Step 3: Integrate karein
\[= \dfrac{1}{2}\Bigg[\dfrac{(x^{2} + 9)^{\frac{1}{2}}}{\frac{1}{2}}\Bigg]_{0}^{\sqrt{7}}\]
\[= \Big[\sqrt{x^{2} + 9}\Big]_{0}^{\sqrt{7}}\]
Kyun: \(n = -\frac{1}{2}\), to \(n + 1 = \frac{1}{2}\). Bahar ka \(\frac{1}{2}\) aur \(\frac{1}{2}\) se divide karna aapas mein kat gaye, aur \(u^{\frac{1}{2}} = \sqrt{u}\).

Step 4: Limits rakhein
\[= \sqrt{7 + 9} - \sqrt{0 + 9}\]
\[= \sqrt{16} - \sqrt{9} = 4 - 3 = 1\]
Kyun: \((\sqrt{7})^{2} = 7\) aur \(0^{2} = 0\). Dekhiye, limit \(\sqrt{7}\) is liye chuni gayi ke \(7 + 9 = 16\) poora square ban jaye aur jawab saaf aaye.

Tasdeeq: antiderivative ka derivative lein, integrand wapas aana chahiye.
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\sqrt{x^{2} + 9} = \dfrac{2x}{2\sqrt{x^{2} + 9}}\]
\[= \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{x^{2} + 9}}\;\checkmark\]

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
Agar upper limit \(\sqrt{7}\) ki jagah 4 hoti to jawab kya aata? Andaza lagaiye, phir check kijiye: \(\sqrt{16 + 9} - \sqrt{9} = 5 - 3 = 2\).
Aur agar upper aur lower limit aapas mein badal dein, yani \(\int_{\sqrt{7}}^{0}\), to jawab \(-1\) ho jayega. Kyun? Kyun ke ab \(F(0) - F(\sqrt{7}) = 3 - 4\) hai. Yeh baat agle sabaq mein Property-II ban kar aayegi.

blocks.title: Substitution in a Definite Integral (Change of variables)
blocks.text:
Suppose that \(g\) is differentiable function on \([a, b]\). Also suppose that \(f\) is continuous on the range of \(g\). Then
\[\int_{a}^{b} f\big(g(x)\big)\,g'(x)\,dx\]
\[= \int_{g(a)}^{g(b)} f(u)\,du.\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yeh wahi substitution hai jo 3.3 mein seekhi thi, bas ek kaam zyada: limits bhi badalni hain. Agar \(u = g(x)\) rakha to
jab \(x = a\), to \(u = g(a)\) (nayi lower limit);
jab \(x = b\), to \(u = g(b)\) (nayi upper limit).
Is ke baad poora integral \(u\) mein hai aur \(x\) mein wapas jaane ki zaroorat nahi. Misaal: jaise rupay ko dollar mein badlein to qeemat ke saath saath shuru aur aakhir ki raqam bhi dollar mein likhni parti hai; aadha rupay aadha dollar nahi chalta.
Yeh tareeqa kab? Jab integrand mein koi function \(g(x)\) aur saath us ka derivative \(g'(x)\) bhi maujood ho.

Ab dekhte hain ke substitution wala box amal mein kaise kaam karta hai. Is misaal mein sab se ahem baat limits ka badalna hai. Ghor se dekhiye ke \(x\) ki limits 0 aur 2 thin, magar \(u\) ki limits 0 aur 4 ban jati hain. Agar yeh qadam bhool gaye to jawab \(e^{2} - 1\) aa jayega jo bilkul ghalat hai.

blocks.title: Example 47
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int_{0}^{2} 2x\,e^{x^{2}}\,dx\).
Maloom karna: is ki value.
Tareeqa: definite integral mein substitution. Power mein \(x^{2}\) baitha hai aur bahar us ka derivative \(2x\) maujood hai. Is liye \(u = x^{2}\) rakhenge aur limits bhi \(u\) mein badal denge.

Step 1: \(g\) aur \(f\) pehchanein
\[g(x) = x^{2},\quad g'(x) = 2x\]
\[e^{x^{2}} \cdot 2x = f\big(g(x)\big)\cdot g'(x)\]
\[\text{with } f(u) = e^{u}\]
Kyun: box wala formula tab lagta hai jab integrand \(f(g(x))\,g'(x)\) ki shakal mein ho. Yahan bilkul yahi shakal hai: \(f\) exponential hai aur andar \(g(x) = x^{2}\).

Step 2: Nayi limits
\[x = 0:\ u = g(0) = 0^{2} = 0\]
\[x = 2:\ u = g(2) = 2^{2} = 4\]
Kyun: ab variable \(u\) hai, to limits bhi \(u\) ki honi chahiye. Purani limits 0 aur 2, \(x\) ki thin.

Step 3: \(u\) mein integrate karein
\[\int_{0}^{2} 2x\,e^{x^{2}}\,dx = \int_{u=0}^{u=4} e^{u}\,du\]
\[= \Big[e^{u}\Big]_{0}^{4} = e^{4} - e^{0}\]
\[= e^{4} - 1\]
Kyun: \(e^{u}\) ka integral khud \(e^{u}\) hai, aur \(e^{0} = 1\). Dekhiye, \(x\) mein wapas jaane ki zaroorat nahi pari.

Tasdeeq: limits badle baghair \(x\) mein antiderivative \(e^{x^{2}}\) hai (is ka derivative chain rule se \(2x\,e^{x^{2}}\) hai).
\[\Big[e^{x^{2}}\Big]_{0}^{2} = e^{4} - e^{0} = e^{4} - 1\;\checkmark\]
Number mein \(e^{4} - 1 \approx 53.598\).

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
Hamari taraf se misaal: \(\int_{0}^{1} 3x^{2}(x^{3} + 1)^{2}\,dx\) kaise karenge? \(u = x^{3} + 1\) rakhiye; \(x = 0\) par \(u = 1\), aur \(x = 1\) par \(u = 2\). To integral \(\int_{1}^{2} u^{2}\,du = \frac{8 - 1}{3} = \frac{7}{3}\) ban jata hai.
Dekha? Limits badal di gayin, is liye aakhir mein \(x\) wapas laane ki zaroorat hi nahi pari.

blocks.title: Integration by Parts Formula for Definite Integrals
blocks.text:
Let \(f(x)\) and \(g(x)\) be functions with continuous derivatives on the interval \([a, b]\). Then the integration by parts formula for definite integrals is:
\[\int_{a}^{b} f(x)g(x)\,dx\]
\[= \Big[f(x)\Big(\int g(x)\,dx\Big)\Big]_{a}^{b}\]
\[\; - \int_{a}^{b}\Big[\Big(\int g(x)\,dx\Big)f'(x)\Big]dx\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yeh 3.4 wala integration by parts hi hai: pehla function \(\times\) doosre ka integral, minus (doosre ka integral \(\times\) pehle ka derivative) ka integral. Farq sirf itna hai ke pehla hissa poora integrate ho chuka hota hai, is liye usi waqt \(a\) aur \(b\) par evaluate kar dete hain.
Aksar yeh evaluate kiya hua hissa zero ho jata hai, kyun ke koi factor dono limits par zero hota hai. Example 48 mein yahi jaadu dekhenge.
Khud sochiye: \(\int_{0}^{1} x\,e^{x}\,dx\) kitna hai? (Hamari taraf se misaal: \(\big[x e^{x}\big]_{0}^{1} - \int_{0}^{1} e^{x}\,dx = e - (e - 1) = 1\).)

Aakhri misaal thori mukhtalif hai: is mein koi number nahi nikalna balke ek baat saabit (prove) karni hai. Function \(f\) ka formula bhi nahi diya, sirf itna bataya hai ke \(f(0)\) aur \(f(\pi)\) zero hain. Aise sawalon mein hamesha socho ke di hui maloomat kahan kaam aayegi. Yahan woh integration by parts ke evaluate wale hisse ko zero karne mein kaam aayegi.

blocks.title: Example 48
blocks.problem: If \(f(0) = f(\pi) = 0\), show that \(\int_{0}^{\pi} f(x)\sin x\,dx = -\int_{0}^{\pi} f''(x)\sin x\,dx\)
steps:
Diya gaya: \(f(0) = f(\pi) = 0\) (aur \(f\) ke derivatives \(f''\) tak continuous hain).
Maloom karna (saabit karna): \(\int_{0}^{\pi} f(x)\sin x\,dx = -\int_{0}^{\pi} f''(x)\sin x\,dx\).
Tareeqa: integration by parts do dafa. Pehli dafa \(f\) pehla function aur \(\sin x\) doosra; doosri dafa \(f'\) pehla aur \(\cos x\) doosra. Hum dekhenge ke evaluate kiye hue hisse zero ho jate hain, kyun ke \(f(0) = f(\pi) = 0\) diya hai aur \(\sin 0 = \sin\pi = 0\) hai.

Step 1: Pehli dafa integration by parts
\[\int_{0}^{\pi} f(x)\sin x\,dx\]
\[= \Big[f(x)(-\cos x)\Big]_{0}^{\pi}\]
\[\; - \int_{0}^{\pi} f'(x)(-\cos x)\,dx\]
Kyun: \(f\) ka integral humein maloom nahi, magar \(\sin x\) ka maloom hai: \(\int \sin x\,dx = -\cos x\). Is liye \(f\) ko pehla function banaya, jis ka sirf derivative lena parta hai.

Step 2: Evaluate kiya hua hissa
\[\Big[-f(x)\cos x\Big]_{0}^{\pi}\]
\[= -f(\pi)\cos\pi + f(0)\cos 0\]
\[= -(0)(-1) + (0)(1) = 0\]
Yani \(\int_{0}^{\pi} f(x)\sin x\,dx = \int_{0}^{\pi} f'(x)\cos x\,dx\).
Kyun: \(f(\pi) = f(0) = 0\) diya hua hai, aur \(\cos\pi = -1\), \(\cos 0 = 1\). Zero ko kisi bhi number se zarb dein, zero hi aata hai. Aur aakhri integral se pehle do minus (\(-\) aur \(-\cos x\) wala) mil kar plus ban gaye.
Dhyan dein: yahan sign ka khayal rakhein; minus minus plus hota hai.

Step 3: Doosri dafa integration by parts
\[\int_{0}^{\pi} f'(x)\cos x\,dx\]
\[= \Big[f'(x)\sin x\Big]_{0}^{\pi}\]
\[\; - \int_{0}^{\pi} \sin x \cdot f''(x)\,dx\]
Kyun: ab \(f'\) pehla function aur \(\cos x\) doosra; \(\int \cos x\,dx = \sin x\), aur \(f'\) ka derivative \(f''\) hai.

Step 4: Evaluate kiya hua hissa phir zero
\[f'(\pi)\sin\pi - f'(0)\sin 0\]
\[= f'(\pi)(0) - f'(0)(0) = 0\]
Kyun: \(\sin\pi = 0\) aur \(\sin 0 = 0\). Mazay ki baat: humein \(f'(\pi)\) ya \(f'(0)\) ki value maloom hi nahi, phir bhi koi farq nahi parta, kyun ke unhein zero se zarb ho rahi hai.

Step 5: Sab hisse jor dein
\[\int_{0}^{\pi} f(x)\sin x\,dx\]
\[= 0 + 0 - \int_{0}^{\pi} f''(x)\sin x\,dx\]
\[= -\int_{0}^{\pi} f''(x)\sin x\,dx\]
Kyun: Step 2 ne bataya ke asal integral \(\int_{0}^{\pi} f'(x)\cos x\,dx\) ke barabar hai, aur Step 4 ne use \(-\int_{0}^{\pi} f''(x)\sin x\,dx\) bana diya.

Tasdeeq (hamari taraf se misaal): \(f(x) = x(\pi - x)\) lein. Is mein \(f(0) = 0\), \(f(\pi) = 0\), aur \(f''(x) = -2\).
\[\int_{0}^{\pi} x(\pi - x)\sin x\,dx = 4\]
\[-\int_{0}^{\pi} (-2)\sin x\,dx = 2\big[-\cos x\big]_{0}^{\pi} = 4\]
Dono taraf 4. \(\checkmark\)
blocks.answer: Saabit ho gaya: \(\int_{0}^{\pi} f(x)\sin x\,dx = -\int_{0}^{\pi} f''(x)\sin x\,dx\).

blocks.text: Chaliye aaj ke sabaq ko ek nazar mein dohrate hain. Definite integral ka matlab hai antiderivative mein do limits rakh kar farq nikalna. Pehli theorem ne bataya ke integration aur differentiation ek doosre ke ulat hain; doosri theorem ne humein hisaab lagane ka tareeqa diya. Phir hum ne dekha ke substitution mein limits badalni hain, aur integration by parts mein pehla hissa foran limits par evaluate hota hai. Agle sabaq 3.6.1 mein hum definite integrals ki properties seekhenge, jo bahut se lambe sawalon ko do teen line ka bana deti hain.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(\int_{a}^{b} f(x)\,dx = F(b) - F(a)\), jahan \(F' = f\). Jawab ek number hai; \(+c\) nahi likhte.
2. First FTC (Theorem 3.2): \(\frac{d}{dx}\int_{a}^{x} f(t)\,dt = f(x)\); differentiation aur integration ek doosre ko undo karte hain.
3. Second FTC (Theorem 3.3): antiderivative nikalo, phir upar wali value minus neeche wali value.
4. Substitution \(u = g(x)\): limits ko \(g(a)\) aur \(g(b)\) mein badlo aur \(u\) mein hi raho.
5. Integration by parts: \(\big[\text{first} \times \int\text{second}\big]_{a}^{b} - \int_{a}^{b}\big(\int\text{second}\big)\times(\text{first})'\,dx\); evaluate wala hissa aksar zero ho jata hai.
6. Jawab: Example 44: 2; Example 45: \(\ln 2\); Example 46: 1; Example 47: \(e^{4} - 1\).

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Ulti tafreeq, yani \(F(a) - F(b)\). Hamesha upar wali limit ki value minus neeche wali.
2. \(F(a)\) ka bracket bhool jana: \(\frac{5}{6} + 1 - \frac{5}{6} - 1\) likh dena, jab ke sahi \(\frac{5}{6} + 1 - \frac{5}{6} + 1\) hai.
3. \(u = g(x)\) rakh kar bhi purani \(x\) wali limits rakhe rehna.
4. Definite integral ke jawab mein \(+c\) likh dena.
5. \((-1)^{\frac{6}{5}}\) ko negative ya 'nahi nikal sakta' samajhna. \(-1\) ka real fifth root \(-1\) hai, aur us ki power 6 se 1 aata hai.
6. Integration by parts mein pehle hisse ko limits par evaluate karna bhool jana.
